Yes—several supplied papers are directly about reinforcement learning with self-play in strategy games. For board and strategy games, self-play RL is used to reach strong or superhuman play in Generals.io, a real-time strategy game [1], Tablut, an asymmetric board game via an AlphaZero-style setup [2], and Stratego, where self-play RL plus search handles large hidden information and achieves superhuman results [3].

They differ in the game challenges and the self-play setup. Generals.io uses plain policy-gradient self-play with sparse win/loss reward and studies training ingredients like parameter averaging and highest-advantage sample selection [1]. Tablut focuses on asymmetry, using separate policy and value heads for each role and stabilization methods such as larger replay buffers and games against past checkpoints [2]. Stratego emphasizes imperfect information and combines self-play RL with test-time search, with the same approach also working in Hanabi and dou dizhu [3].
